turn_text: I think that in terms of bipartisan dialogue when I got to Congress in 2015, that was probably rock bottom. There were no conversations happening between Republicans and Democrats about this issue. And it's interesting as Chelsea brings up denialism, which gets a lot of attention from the media. And certainly there are some climate deniers who are in the Republican Party, but That wasn't the great challenge as far as I was concerned. The great challenge was apathy. Most of the colleagues that I spoke to understood the science, they did not contest it, but they didn't sense any urgency whatsoever. They didn't feel the need to have any impetus whatsoever in dealing with this issue. And certainly they perceived great political risk especially those who had served with you, right? So that was really the greatest obstacle.
